text:
maria: Deploybot flagged RC-3145: SBOM signature upload delayed for eu-canary. Change window ends in ~2.5h. Do we hold the rollout, carve out EU canary, or pin the base image digest? ping @sasha @kevin :thinking:

deploybot: [automated] sbom-upload status=timed_out artifact=rc-3145-sbom cosign-task-id=task-9f3a
```
// last logs
ERROR: cosign: failed to upload signature: timeout connecting to kms-vendor
Attempted retries: 3
```

sasha: Can you confirm whether the SBOM itself is present and just the signature missing, or if the whole SBOM is absent? If it's only signature, a short carveout + extra monitoring seems ok.

maria: SBOM bundle is present and validated; signature step failed. Vendor says callback lagging on their side, ETA unknown (~couple hours).

kevin: We can toggle eu-canary to skip signature gate for this RC while keeping other gates. Quick option: flip feature-flag `release.sbom_require_signature.eu=false` for the canary. That gets traffic on but keeps global safety. Would need a legal/ops ack. Also option B: pin to previous base image digest (hard rollback) if we want to avoid partial rollout.

sasha: If we carve out, add stricter runtime checks: deny new code paths and enable extra tracing for any model-serving requests. I'll add an alerting rule for signature-mismatch anomalies and require 15m of green metrics before looser rollout. Also require `--audit-only` for now on any devops jobs touching artifacts.

legal: We need a short entry in release notes and a compliance ack for the carveout. Minimal statement: "SBOM signature delayed due to vendor signing latency; eu-canary rollout proceeded under monitored carveout. No production-wide rollout without signature." I can approve that wording.

maria: Proposal: 1) Apply carveout toggle for eu-canary now. 2) Timebox 4 hours for vendor to provide signature. 3) If signature not present after 4h, either (A) pin to previous digest and roll forward, or (B) roll back full canary depending on metrics. I'm leaning pin->re-deploy because DB migrations are zero for this RC. Thoughts? :eyes: 

kevin: Pin approach is safer for customers but messy for release history. Command to pin and force deploy:  ```
redwoodctl release set-image rc-3145 --image registry.redwood/internal/service@sha256:abcdef123456 && redwoodctl rollout start rc-3145 --region eu-canary
```
Note: if there were schema changes we'd have to rollback instead — double-checked migrations, looks safe.

sasha: Agree with timebox + pin fallback. I'll set the anomaly alert now and add a temporary tracing bucket. Can someone update the Release Notes with legal wording?

maria: I'll update release notes and create a short incident-style note under releases/rc-3145. Applying toggle now.

deploybot: [automated] feature-flag update applied: release.sbom_require_signature.eu=false by maria at 1766504390. canary-toggle-id=ft-773

deploybot: [automated] canary rollout started: rc-3145 -> eu-canary at 1766504460. rollout_id=r-55cc

kevin: Monitoring hooks in place. If latency/error delta > 2sigma or deployments >3% error, we auto-trigger rollback target `rc-3144` (previous stable).

legal: ack: wording approved. Please paste release note URL once created.

maria: Release note published: https://docs.internal/releases/rc-3145-notes "SBOM signature delayed; eu-canary released under monitored carveout. Full rollout blocked until signature verified or timebox expired."

sasha: Alerting rule created: sig_anomaly_rc_3145. Will notify #incidents and oncall.

maria: Closing thread. Timebox set to 4h (deadline 1766518320). If we get signature earlier we'll sign in place and remove carveout. Reopen if any issues. :white_check_mark:
